transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Tomás Rivera (BrightWave Head of ML), Aisha Patel (BrightWave Platform Eng), Ben Cole (BrightWave Security)

Summary: Quick weekly POC check-in focusing on onboarding progress, staging environment access, and a safety/credentials checklist. Agreed next steps around SOC2 docs, KMS, and scheduling a focused latency benchmark using BrightWave's test harness. Some minor misconfiguration on the peering side discovered; workaround discussed.

Topics: onboarding status; network peering and staging creds; KMS/encryption; latency vs cost expectations; benching plan and roll-forward triggers.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone hi, um, thanks for jumping on, we'll kick off the 10/2 pilot update — quick note on agenda — 1) access and peering, 2) bench plan, 3) security checklist.
[00:18] Tomás Rivera: hey Maya, thanks, quick note — we had a, uh, small hiccup with the peering route leaking, so our test pods couldn't reach the gateway last night, but we fixed a route on our side.
[00:30] Aisha Patel: yeah that was me, I forgot a route table entry, so staging couldn't talk to the redwood gateway, we patched it around 10pm.
[00:44] Diego Alvarez: okay good to know, do you still see any TCP resets? any packet drops at the firewall?
[00:50] Aisha Patel: small amount, um, maybe 0.5% RSTs during the window, not now.
[01:02] Ben Cole: from the security perspective we just want to confirm the handshake is mTLS and cert rotation timeline, where's the docs for that?
[01:10] Maya Chen: yes, we use mutual TLS for the gateway — I'll share the cert rotation cadence, and Diego can add notes about bootstrap tokens.
[01:20] Diego Alvarez: quick add — for POC we recommend short lived tokens and SSO-backed service accounts, also we support customer-managed KMS keys or Redwood KMS, depends on your compliance.
[01:35] Tomás Rivera: okay that's helpful. For the benchmark, our main success criteria is 95th percentile p95 under 250ms for single-shot text gen at 512 tokens, and cost target is roughly $0.0009 per token. Is that realistic?
[01:52] Diego Alvarez: um, so p95 250ms is aggressive for 512 tokens depending on model and quant — with our hosted small-ops models maybe, but for larger ones you'll see higher latency. We can run the bench with a few model variants and report tail latencies.
[02:08] Maya Chen: also note we have dedupe and prefix caching, if your workload has repeated prefixes that helps a lot.
[02:16] Tomás Rivera: yeah some prompts are templated, so cache might help.
[02:24] Aisha Patel: on the peering note, what ports must be open? we assumed 443 and 50051 for grpc.
[02:30] Diego Alvarez: 443 for HTTPS, and we do support gRPC over 443 too, but the control plane agent needs outbound 5222 for telemetry in some setups — I'll confirm.
[02:46] Ben Cole: can you confirm data at rest encryption if we use customer KMS? any extra audit log hooks?
[02:53] Maya Chen: if you bring your KMS we integrate via standard envelopes and we push audit events into the console — for enterprise we can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3.
[03:05] Tomás Rivera: great. Quick status check: Aisha, can you confirm staging creds are in?
[03:12] Aisha Patel: we have partial creds, the API key works but the peering IP list was missing one CIDR, so we couldn't hit the inference nodes.
[03:20] Maya Chen: ok we'll accept that; Diego, any fast remediation?
[03:25] Diego Alvarez: for now add the CIDR and restart the agent, also if you see KV cache misses that's probably because the model variant changed; we pushed a lightweight config overnight that changed cache keys slightly.
[03:40] Tomás Rivera: ah maybe that's why we saw higher token counts.
[03:43] Aisha Patel: yeah token counts jumped 12% during the window.
[03:48] Diego Alvarez: ok we'll roll that config back if you prefer, or we can re-run the caching warmup.
[03:55] Tomás Rivera: let's warm up first, roll back only if we still see regressions.
[04:02] Maya Chen: good call.
[04:08] — brief silence / typing —
[04:25] Maya Chen: switching to bench plan, Diego, can you outline the steps and the artifacts you'll need?
[04:33] Diego Alvarez: sure — we'll need the test harness (curl/grpc script or k6 load profile), sample prompt set (200–500 prompts), expected concurrency, and we prefer a trace token for each run to tie logs to metrics. We'll run 1) cold run with KV empty, 2) warm run after 15 minutes of warmup, 3) tail-latency capture for 30 minutes at target qps.
[04:56] Aisha Patel: for concurrency we plan 10 qps initially, we can scale to 50 later.
[05:03] Diego Alvarez: perfect. Also let us know if you want dedicated capacity vs hosted — dedicated gives more consistent p95 but costs more.
[05:12] Tomás Rivera: cost is a concern, maybe we start hosted and if variance is too high we request a dedicated pool for peak.
[05:22] Ben Cole: security question — is log redaction automatic? we don't want PHI in the logs.
[05:29] Maya Chen: we have automatic PII redaction filters and can configure custom scrubbers; for health data we recommend end-to-end redaction on the client and also post-processing masks.
[05:42] Aisha Patel: okay, want to see the redact config.
[05:45] Maya Chen: I'll include sample redact rules.
[05:48] — 00:06:00 marker —
[06:00] Tomás Rivera: on timeline, we want a go/no-go decision by Oct 20, so we need bench results and security sign-off a week prior, ideally Oct 13.
[06:13] Maya Chen: noted — we can aim to have a bench summary by Oct 11 if test harness is ready by Oct 9.
[06:22] Diego Alvarez: small note about throughput: if you send large batch requests that'll change cost math, we typically measure per-token costs with batch size 1 first.
[06:34] Tomás Rivera: ok we'll stick to single-shot for initial pass.
[06:40] Ben Cole: about SSO — we use Okta for SAML, should be straightforward?
[06:45] Maya Chen: yes we have an Okta SAML integration guide, we'll share the SAML metadata and example assertions.
[06:55] Aisha Patel: one more infra issue — our CI runs the harness from inside a bastion; do you allow IP allowlist for a dynamic bastion?
[07:03] Diego Alvarez: we can support CIDR ranges or short-lived IP allow lists; for dynamic bastions we prefer a VPN peering or a proxy that mTLS to keep the security posture.
[07:17] Tomás Rivera: anything on observability — how granular are traces? can we get token-level cost breakdowns?
[07:24] Maya Chen: yes in the console we show token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns, and a trace ID mapping to requests. Diego can demo the console next call.
[07:35] Diego Alvarez: quick note — our observability exports include span-level timing but occasionally model names get slightly garbled in the agent logs (transcription of model name 'redwood/small-v2' appears as 'redwood small two' sometimes) — just a minor labeling quirk.
[07:55] Tomás Rivera: ha okay, not a blocker.
[08:03] — 00:15:00 marker —
[15:05] Aisha Patel: from ops, we need the exact list of ports and egress destinations to open, can that be a single doc?
[15:12] Maya Chen: yes I'll send a network matrix and a minimal port list.
[15:20] Ben Cole: we'll need a copy of your SOC2 and ISO statements, and evidence for encryption at rest, can you share a redacted manager report?
[15:29] Maya Chen: we can share our SOC2 summary and an attestation, for deep dives we'll route through legal NDA.
[15:35] Tomás Rivera: on KMS, if we use customer keys what's the perf penalty?
[15:40] Diego Alvarez: negligible per request after the envelope scheme; it adds a small latency on key unwrap during model load, not per-token.
[15:50] Aisha Patel: noted.
[15:56] Maya Chen: ok let's review the immediate blockers — 1) staging peering CIDR missing (fixed, confirm by Aisha), 2) KV cache warmup mismatch (Diego to re-run warmup), 3) redact rules sample (Maya to send).
[16:12] Aisha Patel: confirm CIDR added and agent restarted, we'll validate test calls in next hour.
[16:18] Diego Alvarez: I'll queue cache warmup tonight and report metrics.
[16:23] Ben Cole: I'll compile the security Qs and send by EOD tomorrow.
[16:30] Tomás Rivera: good.
[16:33] — brief crosstalk —
[16:45] Maya Chen: ok last bit — pricing conversation, we covered rough per-token target earlier, want to note that discounts for committed volume are available, and dedicated pools have separate contract terms.
[16:58] Tomás Rivera: understood, we'll surface CTL for committed volume numbers with finance.
[17:07] Maya Chen: great. Any other questions?
[17:12] Aisha Patel: none from ops.
[17:15] Ben Cole: none from security.
[17:18] Tomás Rivera: all good.
[17:22] Maya Chen: recap: I'll share SOC2 + network matrix + sample redact rules; Diego will share bench runbook and warmup results; Aisha will validate peering and send confirmation — target bench run next week.
[17:38] — Meeting ends —

Notes on transcription: occasional misheard terms (e.g., 'KV cache' rendered as 'kay-vee cache', 'mTLS' sometimes as 'mtls' lowercase). Some overlapping talk around 03:40 — 03:55.
